title: Total order value
prompt: Define `order_total(prices, quantities)` returning the sum of price * quantity for paired lists. Return 0 for empty lists.

title: Clean a name
prompt: Define `clean_name(s)` that strips surrounding whitespace and returns the name in Title Case, collapsing repeated inner spaces to one.
hints: str.split() with no arguments splits on any whitespace run.

title: Word frequency
prompt: Define `word_freq(text)` returning a dict of lowercase word -> count. Split on whitespace and ignore case.

title: Unique and sorted
prompt: Define `unique_sorted(items)` returning a sorted list of the distinct items.

title: Group by key
prompt: Define `group_by(rows, key)` where rows is a list of dicts. Return a dict mapping each value of `key` to the list of rows having it, preserving input order.

title: Safe integer parsing
prompt: Define `to_int(value, default=None)` that converts a value to int and returns `default` if conversion fails (ValueError or TypeError).

title: Retry decorator
prompt: Write a decorator factory `retry(times)` that calls the wrapped function up to `times` times, retrying only when it raises an exception, and re-raises the last exception if all attempts fail. Use functools.wraps.
hints: A decorator factory returns a decorator which returns a wrapper.
Track the last exception and raise it after the loop.
expected: A function failing twice then succeeding returns normally with retry(3).

title: Generator: read in batches
prompt: Define `batches(iterable, size)` as a generator yielding lists of `size` items (the last batch may be shorter). It must not build the whole input in memory.
hints: Accumulate into a list; yield when it reaches `size`.
Yield any remainder after the loop.

title: Read a CSV
prompt: `sales.csv` is in the working directory. Using the csv module, create a variable `rows` (list of dicts) and `total_revenue` = sum of quantity * unit_price over all rows (floats).
hints: csv.DictReader yields dicts; values are strings - convert them.
starter:
import csv

# build rows and total_revenue

title: Revenue by category
prompt: Read `sales.csv` and build `by_category`: a dict category -> total revenue (quantity * unit_price), rounded to 2 decimals.

title: Parse log levels
prompt: `app.log` contains log lines. Build `level_counts`: a dict of log level (the 3rd whitespace-separated token: INFO, WARNING, ERROR) -> number of lines.
hints: Read lines, skip blank ones, line.split()[2].

title: Flatten nested JSON orders
prompt: `orders.json` has an `orders` list with nested `customer` and `items`. Build `flat`: one dict per order with keys `order_id`, `customer`, `tier`, `item_count`, `total` (sum of qty*price over items).
hints: Use .get / sum over items; orders without items have total 0.

title: Paginated API simulation
prompt: Network access is disabled, so a fake API is provided: `fetch_page(page)` returns {'data': [...], 'next_page': int or None}. Define `fetch_all()` that follows `next_page` until it is None and returns all records as one list.
hints: Loop while page is not None.
Extend the result with each page's data.

title: Clean dirty customers (stdlib)
prompt: Read `customers_dirty.csv` with csv. Build `clean`: a list of dicts with keys id (int), name (trimmed, Title Case), email (lowercase), country (uppercase). Skip rows with a blank name and drop exact duplicate ids (keep the first).
hints: Track seen ids in a set.

title: pandas: total by customer
prompt: With pandas, load `sales.csv` into DataFrame `df`, add a `revenue` column (quantity * unit_price) and create `top` = a Series of revenue summed per `customer`, sorted descending.

title: pandas: clean missing values
prompt: Load `customers_dirty.csv` with pandas into `df`. Drop duplicate rows, convert `age` to numeric (invalid -> NaN) and fill missing ages with the median age of valid ones. Keep result in `df`.
expected: No duplicates, no NaN in age, age numeric

title: pandas: month-over-month
prompt: Load `sales.csv` into `df`, parse `order_date` as dates, compute revenue (quantity*unit_price) and create `monthly`: a DataFrame with columns `month` (like '2024-01') and `revenue`, one row per month in chronological order.

title: numpy: normalise
prompt: Using numpy, define `min_max(arr)` that scales an array to the range 0-1: (x - min) / (max - min). If all values are equal return zeros.

title: A reusable Validator class
prompt: Define class `Validator` with `__init__(self, required)` (list of required field names) and method `validate(self, record)` returning a list of error strings: one `'missing: <field>'` per field that is absent or empty (None or '').
hints: Loop over self.required and check record.get(field).

title: Mini ETL: extract, transform, load
prompt: Write `run_etl(rows)`: transform a list of dicts {'id','amount'} by dropping rows where amount is None or negative, converting amount to float, and dropping duplicate ids (keep first). Load into an in-memory sqlite3 table `facts(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, amount REAL)` and return the sqlite3 connection.
hints: Transform first, then executemany an INSERT.
expected: run_etl([...]) returns a connection with cleaned rows

title: Idempotent upsert
prompt: Define `upsert(conn, rows)` where conn has table `t(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, val TEXT)`. Insert (id, val) tuples, updating val when the id already exists. Running it twice with the same rows must leave the same data.
hints: SQLite supports INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET val = excluded.val.
expected: Re-running does not duplicate or fail.

title: Incremental watermark
prompt: Define `new_records(records, watermark)` returning (new, new_watermark): records are dicts with ISO string field `updated_at`; return those strictly greater than the watermark (string compare is fine for ISO format) and the maximum updated_at seen (or the old watermark if none).
expected: Only rows after the watermark; watermark advances.

title: Logging a pipeline step
prompt: Define `run_step(fn, name)` that calls fn(), logs with the logging module (logger name `etl`) an INFO message `step <name> started` and `step <name> finished`, and on exception logs ERROR `step <name> failed` and returns None instead of raising. Return fn's result on success.
starter:
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger('etl')

def run_step(fn, name):
    pass
expected: Success returns the value; failure returns None and logs an error.

title: Debug: off-by-one in a window
prompt: The function below should return the average of each sliding window of size `k` but is buggy. Fix it so `rolling_mean([1,2,3,4], 2) == [1.5, 2.5, 3.5]`.
hints: How many windows exist in a list of length n? n - k + 1.

title: Context manager timer
prompt: Write a context manager class `Timer` that records elapsed seconds into attribute `elapsed` on exit (use time.perf_counter). `with Timer() as t: ...` then `t.elapsed >= 0`.
expected: t.elapsed is a non-negative float after the block
